summary: Source-based expansion of Quillen and Waldhausen K-theory and its nonconnective extension. For exact categories: Quillen's Q-construction with its universal property and the proof that π₁BQM is K₀M; the definition and elementary properties of K_i (Quillen 1973 §2; Weibel IV §6); the + = Q theorem for split exact categories via the extension category EA and Theorem B (Weibel IV §7); additivity via Theorem A, the resolution and dévissage theorems, and the full proof of the localization theorem for Serre subcategories (Quillen §§3–5; Weibel V §§3–5); cofinality with its degree-zero correction. For Waldhausen categories: the axioms and the S.-construction with its induced cofibrations (Weibel II §9, IV §8; Waldhausen §1.3), Waldhausen's additivity theorem from simplicial Theorems A/B (Waldhausen §1.4, image-checked pages), the relative S.-construction fibration and delooping (§1.5; Weibel V.1.7), Waldhausen localization and approximation (Weibel V §2; Schlichting App. A) and the Gillet–Waldhausen comparison. Relative groups and the excision boundary (Weibel IV 1.11). Schlichting's negative K-theory of Frobenius pairs: set-up, localization in negative degrees, the flasque countable envelope and suspension, the nonconnective spectrum, derived-equivalence invariance, agreement and vanishing theorems. Morita/colimit invariance and biexact products are recorded with their unread imports. Several imported proofs (Waldhausen §1.6 and 1.9, Suslin excision, Thomason–Trobaugh fundamental theorem, product coherence) remain unread and are listed as gaps.

nodes.title: Exact categories and Quillen's category QM
nodes.statement: An exact category is an additive category M with a family E of short sequences M′ ↣ M ↠ M″ such that (a) E is closed under isomorphism and contains the split sequences, and in each sequence i is a kernel of j and j a cokernel of i; (b) admissible epimorphisms are closed under composition and base change by arbitrary maps, admissible monomorphisms under composition and cobase change; (c) if M → M″ has a kernel and N → M → M″ is an admissible epimorphism for some N → M, then M → M″ is an admissible epimorphism, and dually. QM has the objects of M; a morphism M → M′ is an isomorphism class (isomorphisms inducing the identity on M and M′, unique when they exist) of diagrams M ↞ N ↣ M′ with an admissible epimorphism and an admissible monomorphism, composed by fibre product. Equivalently a morphism is an admissible layer M₀ ⊂ M₁ ⊂ M′ with an isomorphism M ≅ M₁/M₀. Each morphism factors uniquely up to unique isomorphism as u = i_! j^!, every morphism of QM is a monomorphism, QM/M′ is equivalent to the ordered set of admissible layers of M′, isomorphisms of QM are those of M, and Q(M^op) ≅ QM exchanging injective and surjective arrows.
hypotheses: The isomorphism classes of diagrams M ↞ N ↣ M′ form a set (for example M well-powered); for K-groups one uses a small exact category or an equivalent small subcategory.
Quillen's axioms (a)–(c); Keller's axioms Ex0–Ex2^op are equivalent to them (Schlichting 3.1, citing Keller 1990, not read).
proofSteps: Composition of M ↞ N ↣ M′ and M′ ↞ N′ ↣ M″ uses the fibre product N ×_{M′} N′, whose projection to N is an admissible epimorphism by base change and whose map to N′ is an admissible monomorphism (Quillen §2; Weibel IV Definition 6.1).
Associativity and well-definedness on isomorphism classes follow from the universal property of fibre products (stated as clear by Quillen).
Identify morphisms with admissible layers using the correspondence between admissible subobjects and admissible quotient objects (Quillen §2; Weibel IV Exercise 6.1).
The injective-followed-by-surjective factorization u = j′^! i′_! comes from the bicartesian square of an admissible layer (Quillen §2, LNM p. 101).
Quillen's embedding of M in the abelian category of left exact functors is sketched with details omitted; it is not needed for the definition.
acceptance: Morphisms from 0 to M in QM correspond to admissible subobjects of M (Weibel IV 6.1.2).
For split exact structures on an additive category the admissible epimorphisms are split surjections; do not identify split and nonsplit structures (roadmap test).
Check the pinned Tau Ceti `ExactStructure` fields against (a)–(c) before using it as the carrier (unchecked).

nodes.title: Universal property of QM
nodes.statement: Let M be an exact category and C a category. Suppose given objects hM of C for M in M, maps i_!: hM′ → hM for admissible monomorphisms i: M′ ↣ M and j^!: hM″ → hM for admissible epimorphisms j: M ↠ M″, such that (a) (i′i)_! = i′_! i_!, (jj′)^! = j′^! j^! and identities go to identities, and (b) for every bicartesian square with horizontal admissible monomorphisms and vertical admissible epimorphisms, i_! j′^! = j^! i′_!. Then there is a unique functor QM → C compatible with these operations. In particular an exact functor F: M → M′ induces QF: QM → QM′.
hypotheses: M exact category with QM a category (set-theoretic hypothesis of the preceding node).
proofSteps: Every morphism of QM factors as i_! j^! uniquely up to unique isomorphism, so a functor is determined by its values on injective and surjective arrows.

Relations (a) give functoriality within each class; relation (b) is what is needed for composition: in a composite (i′_! j′^!)(i_! j^!) the middle part j′^! i_! (an injective arrow followed by a surjective one) is rewritten in the normal form i″_! j″^! by the bicartesian square. Quillen only asserts the universal property ('it is clear', LNM p. 102); this argument is packet-authored.
acceptance: The functor F_S used in the proof of π₁BQM = K₀M (F_S(i_!) = id, F_S(j^!) = multiplication by [Ker j]) is constructed by this universal property.
An exact functor induces a functor QM → QM′ and hence K_i(M) → K_i(M′).

nodes.title: π₁(BQM, 0) is the Grothendieck group K₀M
nodes.statement: For a small exact category M with chosen zero object 0, π₁(BQM, 0) is canonically isomorphic to K₀M, the abelian group generated by classes [M] with [M] = [M′] + [M″] for every exact sequence. Under the isomorphism the class [A] is represented by Weibel's based loop 0 ↣ A ↠ 0 (6.2.1), composed of the two edges from 0 to A given by the admissible monomorphism 0 ↣ A and by the admissible epimorphism A ↠ 0 (the QM-morphism 0 ↞ A), the second traversed backwards, and a morphism A ↞ B₂ ↣ B of QM corresponds to the class of the kernel of B₂ ↠ A.
hypotheses: M small exact category, 0 a chosen zero object.
Orientation conventions of the loop must be fixed once; Weibel's representative (6.2.1) is 0 ↣ A ↠ 0, the edge 0 ↣ A followed by the edge 0 ↞ A traversed backwards.
proofSteps: (Quillen) By the covering-space classification (StableHomotopyKTheory H.1), coverings of BQM correspond to morphism-inverting functors F: QM → Sets; it suffices to show the category of such F is equivalent to K₀M-sets via F ↦ F(0).
Replace such F by an isomorphic one with F(0 ↣ M) = identity; call this full subcategory Γ.
Given a K₀M-set S, define F_S(M) = S, F_S(i_!) = id, F_S(j^!) = multiplication by [Ker j], using the universal property of QM.

Conversely, for F in Γ and an exact sequence M′ ↣ M ↠ M″, the bicartesian relation gives F(j_M^!) = F(j_{M′}^!) F(j_{M″}^!) in Aut F(0), so the universal property of K₀M gives a unique homomorphism K₀M → Aut F(0) with [M] ↦ F(j_M^!); the two constructions are inverse isomorphisms of categories.

(Weibel) Alternatively take the maximal tree T = {0 ↣ A}; by the maximal-tree presentation π₁ is generated by the [0 ↞ A] and every relation [f][g] = [f∘g] reduces to the additivity relation [0 ↞ B] = [0 ↞ A][0 ↞ C] coming from 0 ↣ C ↞ B = 0 ↞ A ↣ B.
acceptance: The inverse map K₀M → π₁ is defined by the universal property of K₀ (not by comparing cardinalities), matching the roadmap contract.
K₀M could equally be defined as the possibly nonabelian group on the same generators and relations; the relations force commutativity (Quillen's remark in the proof).
Compatibility with + = Q: the isomorphism identifies [A] with the class of A in K₀(S⁻¹S) (Weibel IV Exercise 7.8).

nodes.title: K-groups of an exact category and their elementary properties
nodes.statement: For a small exact category M, K_i(M) = π_{i+1}(BQM, 0) for i ≥ 0, independent of the zero object; for an exact category with a set of isomorphism classes one uses an equivalent small subcategory, the choice being irrelevant. K_i is a functor from exact categories and exact functors to abelian groups, isomorphic exact functors induce equal maps, K_i(M^op) ≅ K_i(M), K_i(M × M′) ≅ K_iM ⊕ K_iM′ with the sum in K_iM induced by ⊕, and K_i commutes with filtered colimits of exact categories. For a ring A, K_iA = K_i(P(A)); a ring map induces A′ ⊗_A − and K_i(A × A′) = K_iA ⊕ K_iA′, K_i commutes with filtered colimits of rings (using idempotent matrices), and P ↦ Hom_A(P, A) gives K_iA ≅ K_i(A^op). BQM is a homotopy-commutative H-space via ⊕.
hypotheses: Small exact category, or a set of isomorphism classes (equivalent small model).
Filtered colimits are indexed by small filtering categories; for rings the functor A ↦ P(A) is replaced by idempotent matrices so that it is a functor.
proofSteps: A unique map 0 → 0′ in QM gives a canonical path, so the groups do not depend on the zero object (Quillen §2).

Natural isomorphisms of exact functors induce homotopic maps (StableHomotopyKTheory H.1, natural transformations give homotopies); equivalent small models give homotopy equivalent BQ (Weibel IV Exercise 6.2).

Q(M × M′) = QM × QM′ and realization preserves products (compactly generated topology), giving (8); ⊕ induces the group sum because M ↦ M ⊕ 0 and M ↦ 0 ⊕ M are isomorphic to the identity (Quillen §2).
Q commutes with filtered colimits and Proposition 3 of §1 gives (9) (StableHomotopyKTheory H.1 filtered-colimits node).
acceptance: The zero exact category has contractible K-theory (roadmap test).
K_n(M_r(A)) ≅ K_n(A) via Morita equivalence P(A) ≃ P(M_r(A)) (see K.7 node).
Quillen's remark that K₁ of an exact category differs in general from Bass's universal determinant group (Gersten–Murthy examples) must be respected when comparing with K₁ models.

nodes.title: The + = Q theorem for split exact categories
nodes.statement: If A is a split exact category and S = iso A, then ΩBQA ≃ B(S⁻¹S), so K_n(A) ≅ K_n(S) for n ≥ 0. For every ring R, ΩBQP(R) ≃ K₀(R) × BGL(R)⁺ (a space-level description after choosing component representatives), hence K_n(R) = K_nP(R) agrees with π_n BGL(R)⁺ for n ≥ 1. The homotopy fibration used is S⁻¹S → S⁻¹EA → QA, where EA is the category of admissible exact sequences and S acts by A′□(A ↣ B ↠ C) = (A′ ⊕ A ↣ A′ ⊕ B ↠ C).
hypotheses: A split exact: every admissible exact sequence splits; if A has a non-split exact sequence the category ⟨S, E_C⟩ is not connected (Weibel IV Remark 7.5.2). Independently of splitting, Theorem B cannot be applied to EA → QA itself unless A ≅ 0 (Exercise 7.4), which is why the localized functor S⁻¹EA → QA is used.
S = iso A has faithful translations (Weibel IV Exercise 7.1).
proofSteps: Define EA with morphisms the equivalence classes of diagrams (7.3.1); the target functor t: EA → QA is fibred with fibre E_C and base change φ* (Lemma 7.7, Exercise 7.2), and E₀ ≃ S (Example 7.4.1).
Each E_C is symmetric monoidal via (A₁ ⊕ A₂ ↣ B₁ ×_C B₂ ↠ C), with faithful monoidal S → E_C, A ↦ (A ↣ A ⊕ C ↠ C) (Lemma 7.5).

Proposition 7.6: S⁻¹S → S⁻¹E_C → ⟨S, E_C⟩ is a fibration (Exercise 4.7), and L = ⟨S, E_C⟩ is contractible: it is a connected group-like H-space (split exactness) and the diagonal E → E ∗ E gives a homotopy between the identity and multiplication by 2.
Theorem 7.8: S⁻¹EA → QA satisfies Quillen's Theorem B because the base changes for 0 ↣ C and 0 ↞ C compose with S⁻¹S ≃ S⁻¹E_C to A ↦ A and A ↦ A ⊕ C (Exercise 7.5), both homotopy equivalences.
Proof of 7.1: EA ≃ Sub(iQA) is contractible (Exercise 7.3); an action on a contractible category is invertible, so S⁻¹EA is contractible (Exercise 4.6); hence ΩBQA ≃ B(S⁻¹S).
Corollary 7.2 combines this with B(S⁻¹S) ≃ K₀(R) × BGL(R)⁺ for S = iso P(R) (StableHomotopyKTheory H.4 cofinality node).
acceptance: π₁BQA ≅ K₀(S) identifies [A] with [A] (Exercise 7.8); π₂BQA ≅ K₁(S) identifies the class [α] of an automorphism with its class in K₁(iso A) (Exercise 7.9).

For a commutative ring R, the transpose-inverse involution on BGL(R)⁺ agrees via Corollary 7.2 with the canonical involution of QP(R) induced by P ↦ Hom_R(P, R) (Exercise 7.10, stated for commutative R without proof).
Products agree up to basepoint-preserving homotopy (Theorem 7.9) — imported from Waldhausen 1978 9.2.6 and Weibel 1981 4.3, not read.

nodes.title: Additivity: the extension category and characteristic sequences
nodes.statement: Let M be an exact category and E the exact category of short exact sequences in M, with exact functors s, t, q (sub, total, quotient). Then (s, q): QE → QM × QM is a homotopy equivalence. Consequently, for an exact sequence F′ ↣ F ↠ F″ of exact functors M′ → M one has F_* = F′_* + F″_* on K_i; for an admissible filtration 0 = F₀ ⊂ ⋯ ⊂ F_n = F with exact quotients F_*=Σ(F_p/F_{p−1})_*; and for an exact sequence 0 → F₀ → ⋯ → F_n → 0 of exact functors Σ(−1)^p (F_p)_* = 0.
hypotheses: Exact categories with a set of isomorphism classes; the functors in the sequences are exact and the sequences are pointwise exact.
For the filtration corollary the quotient functors F_p/F_{p−1} must be exact.
proofSteps: By Theorem A it suffices that each comma category C = (s, q)/(M, N) of triples (E, u: sE → M, v: qE → N) is contractible (Quillen Theorem 2 proof).

Let C′ ⊂ C be the triples with u surjective and C″ ⊂ C′ those with in addition v injective. The inclusion C′ ⊂ C has a left adjoint by pushing out E along the injective part of u (universal arrow X → X̄, uniqueness via the least admissible layer); C″ ⊂ C′ has a left adjoint by pulling back along the surjective part of v.
Adjoint functors are homotopy equivalences, so C ≃ C″, and C″ has an initial object (0, j_M^!, i_{N!}), so it is contractible.
Corollary 1: the split-sequence functor f: M′ × M″ → E is a section of (s, q), hence t_* = (s_* + q_*) on K-groups; Corollaries 2–3 follow by induction.
Weibel V.1.3 gives an equivalent proof with subcategories T_A, T_C, functors p, q and natural transformations, and T_A ∩ T_C having an initial object.
acceptance: Additivity gives K_iX a module structure over K₀X for vector bundles on a ringed space via (E ⊗ −)_* (Quillen §3 Applications).

For a non-negatively graded ring A = A₀ ⊕ A₁ ⊕ ⋯, K_i(P_gr(A)) ≅ Z[t, t⁻¹] ⊗ K_iA₀ via characteristic filtrations (Quillen §3 Proposition, which also quotes [Bass, p. 637] for the non-canonical decomposition of graded projectives; Weibel V Corollary 1.8.1 for S = R ⊕ S₁ ⊕ S₂ ⊕ ⋯).
Flasque categories (∞ ≅ 1 ⊕ ∞) have contractible K-theory by additivity (Eilenberg swindle, Weibel V 1.9).

nodes.title: Resolution theorem and transfer maps
nodes.statement: Let P be a full exact subcategory of an exact category H, closed under extensions and under kernels of admissible surjections in H, such that every object of H has a finite P-resolution 0 → P_n → ⋯ → P₀ → M → 0. Then QP → QH is a homotopy equivalence and K_i(P) ≅ K_i(H). In particular K_i(A) ≅ K_i(P_∞(A)) for every ring A, K_i(A) ≅ G_i(A) = K_i(Modf(A)) for A noetherian regular, and for a regular noetherian separated scheme K(X) ≃ G(X). If f: A → B is a ring map such that B, as an A-module, lies in P_∞(A) (a finite resolution by finitely generated projective A-modules), restriction of scalars P_∞(B) → P_∞(A) defines transfers f_*: K_iB → K_iA with (gf)_* = f_*g_* when also C ∈ P_∞(B), and, for commutative A and B, the projection formula f_*(f^*x · y) = x · f_*y for x ∈ K₀A and y ∈ K_iB (Quillen §4 (3)–(5)); Weibel V 3.3.2 gives the K_*(R)-module form f_*(x · f^*y) = f_*(x) · y for x ∈ K_*(S), y ∈ K_*(R) using a biexact pairing.
hypotheses: P ⊂ H full, closed under extensions and under kernels of admissible surjections; finite P-resolutions of every object.
Regular means noetherian with every module of finite projective dimension; for schemes separatedness is required (Weibel V Remark 3.4.2 gives a nonseparated counterexample for K₀).

Transfers: B ∈ P_∞(A) as an A-module (finite projective dimension alone is not Quillen's hypothesis; finite generation of the resolving projectives is required); A and B commutative for the projection formula, which Quillen states for x ∈ K₀A.
proofSteps: Reduce to resolutions of length one by the filtration H = ∪H_n with H₀ = P; each H_{n−1} ⊂ H_n is closed under admissible subobjects and extensions (Weibel V Theorem 3.1 proof; Quillen §4 Lemma and Corollary 1).

nodes.title: Dévissage theorem
nodes.statement: Let A ⊂ B be an exact abelian subcategory of an abelian category, closed under subobjects and quotients (and finite products), such that every object of B has a finite filtration with subquotients in A. Then QA → QB is a homotopy equivalence and K_i(A) ≅ K_i(B). If every object of B has finite length, K_i(B) ≅ ⊕_j K_i(D_j) with D_j the opposite endomorphism division rings of representatives of the simple objects. If I is a nilpotent ideal in a noetherian ring A, then G_i(A/I) ≅ G_i(A).
hypotheses: A and B abelian with a set of isomorphism classes; A closed in B under subobjects, quotients and finite products.

Finite filtrations with subquotients in A exist for every object of B; the associated quotient functor need not be exact (Weibel V Example 4.2.1), so admissible-filtration additivity does not replace dévissage.
proofSteps: By Theorem A it suffices that f/M is contractible for every M in B; f/M is equivalent to the ordered set J(M) of layers (M₀, M₁) of M with M₁/M₀ in A (Quillen Theorem 4 proof).
Using the finite filtration, it suffices that J(M′) ⊂ J(M) is a homotopy equivalence when M/M′ is in A.

Define r(M₀, M₁) = (M₀ ∩ M′, M₁ ∩ M′) and s(M₀, M₁) = (M₀ ∩ M′, M₁); these are well defined because A is closed under subobjects and products; ri = id and natural transformations i r ⇐ s ⇒ id give a homotopy inverse (Weibel V Theorem 4.1 proof via adjoints).
Finite-length corollary: reduce to semisimple objects by dévissage, then to one simple object by products and filtered colimits, and use Hom(X, −): A ≃ modules over D = End(X)^op.
acceptance: G_*(Z/p^r) ≅ K_*(F_p) (Weibel V §4 opening).
K_*M_s(R) ≅ G_*(R/sR) for s-torsion modules over a noetherian ring (Weibel V Application 4.4).

nodes.title: Quillen's localization theorem for Serre subcategories
nodes.statement: Let B be a Serre subcategory of a small abelian category A with quotient functor loc: A → A/B. Then K(B) → K(A) → K(A/B) is a homotopy fibration sequence, giving a long exact sequence ⋯ → K_{n+1}(A/B) → K_n(B) → K_n(A) → K_n(A/B) → K_{n−1}(B) → ⋯ ending in K₀(B) → K₀(A) → K₀(A/B) → 0, functorial for exact functors of pairs. For a Dedekind domain A with fraction field F this gives ⋯ → ⊕_m K_i(A/m) → K_iA → K_iF → ⊕_m K_{i−1}(A/m) → ⋯, where the first map is the sum of transfers and the second is induced by A → F.
hypotheses: B ⊂ A Serre subcategory (closed under subobjects, quotients and extensions) of a small abelian category; exact categories that are not abelian are not covered (Quillen's introduction, PDF p. 2: 'the devissage and localization theorems apply only to abelian categories').

The Dedekind corollary also uses the resolution theorem (A regular), dévissage for finite-length torsion modules and [Swan, p. 115] for the equivalence of Modf(A) modulo torsion modules with Modf(F) (not read).
proofSteps: QB → QA → Q(A/B) is constant at 0 on QB, so the map factors through the comma category 0\Q loc; by Theorem B it suffices that (a) every u*: V\Q loc → V′\Q loc is a homotopy equivalence and (b) QB → 0\Q loc is one (Quillen Theorem 5 proof).

Quillen first reduces (a) to the maps i_{V!}: 0 ↣ V: factor u into injective and surjective maps; since passing to the opposite categories does not change the Q-category (§2 (7)) and turns surjective maps of Q(A/B) into injective maps of Q(A°/B°), it suffices to treat u = i_! for i: V′ ↣ V; and since i_! i_{V′!} = i_{V!}, it suffices that every (i_{V!})*: V\Q loc → 0\Q loc is a homotopy equivalence (LNM p. 114).

Lemma 1 (Claims 5.1.2–5.1.3): the full subcategory F_V of pairs (M, u) with u an isomorphism is homotopy equivalent to V\Q loc, since each comma category is a filtering poset of layers, hence contractible; F₀ ≅ QB gives (b).

For N in A, the category E_N of pairs (M, h: M → N) with loc(h) an isomorphism has a kernel functor k_N: E_N → QB; Lemma 2 shows the restriction to epimorphic h is a homotopy equivalence by a left adjoint via pushout and an initial object.

Lemma 3: E′_N ⊂ E_N is a homotopy equivalence by Theorem B's corollary applied to the fibred functor (M, h) ↦ Im h over the poset of subobjects with quotient in B, which has a final object; Lemma 4: isomorphisms mod B induce homotopy equivalences g_* by a natural transformation Ker h ↣ Ker gh.

Lemma 5: F_V is isomorphic to the filtered colimit of E_N over pairs (N, loc N ≅ V), so by Proposition 3 each E_N → F_V is a homotopy equivalence; a homotopy-commutative square then shows (i_{V!})*: V\Q loc → 0\Q loc is a homotopy equivalence, proving (a).

nodes.title: Cofinality with the degree-zero correction
nodes.statement: (Exact categories) If B ⊂ A is an exact subcategory closed under extensions and cofinal (for every A there is A′ with A ⊕ A′ in B), then BQB is homotopy equivalent to the covering space of BQA corresponding to the subgroup K₀(B) ⊂ K₀(A); hence K_n(B) ≅ K_n(A) for n > 0 while K₀(B) may be a proper subgroup. (Waldhausen) If A is strictly cofinal in B then wS.A → wS.B is a homotopy equivalence. (Thomason) For a Waldhausen category A with a cylinder functor satisfying the cylinder axiom and a surjection π: K₀(A) → G, the subcategory B of objects with π[B] = 0 gives a homotopy fibration K(B) → K(A) → G, so K_n(B) ≅ K_n(A) for n > 0 and 0 → K₀(B) → K₀(A) → G → 0 is exact.
hypotheses: Exact case: closure under extensions and cofinality; Waldhausen case: strict cofinality (for every B there is A with B ∨ A isomorphic to an object of A), or cofinality plus closure under extensions and K₀ agreement (Weibel IV 8.9).
Thomason's version needs a cylinder functor with the cylinder axiom (Schlichting A.4 replaces this by factorizations into a cofibration followed by a weak equivalence, with ∅ = 0).
proofSteps: Exact case: Weibel IV Exercise 6.6 (Gersten, stated as an exercise with steps) treats the special case where B consists of the objects with φ[B] = 0 for a surjection φ: K₀(A) → G: the functor ψ: QA → G sending A ↞ B₂ ↣ B to φ[Ker(B₂ ↠ A)] satisfies Theorem B, so B(ψ/*) is the homotopy fibre of BQA → BG; Theorem A gives QB ≃ ψ⁻¹(*), and cofinality gives ψ⁻¹(*) ≃ ψ/*. Weibel says (p. IV.56) that the general case of 6.4.1 follows using Waldhausen cofinality in the form 8.9.1: a cofinal B closed under extensions is contained in B′ = {A : [A] ∈ K₀(B)} with K₀(B) = K₀(B′), so K(B) ≃ K(B′) by IV 8.9 and Exercise 6.6 applies to B′ with G = K₀(A)/K₀(B). This reduction is only indicated in the source.

Waldhausen 1.5.9: reduce by Corollary 1.5.6/1.5.7 to contractibility of wS.F.(B, A); by the realization lemma reduce to strict cofinality of S_nA in S_nB (Assertion 1) and of A(m, w) in B(m, w) (Assertion 2), and prove the simplicial set s.(B, A) contractible by moving finitely many simplices into A with a single added object (Assertion 3).

Weibel IV 8.9 gives the same argument via Lemma 8.9.2 and Grayson's trick; Thomason's version (Weibel V Theorem 2.3) applies Waldhausen localization to the weak equivalences w = {A → A′ : π[A] = π[A′]} together with wS.(A, w) ≃ BG (Weibel IV Theorem 8.10).
acceptance: Free modules are strictly cofinal in stably free modules but not in projective modules (Waldhausen p. 346).
Idempotent completion: an exact category is cofinal in its idempotent completion, and K₀ can change while positive K-groups agree (Weibel IV Exercise 8.13; Schlichting 5.5).
Do not state K₀ agreement for a merely cofinal subcategory.

nodes.title: Waldhausen categories and the S.-construction with induced cofibrations
nodes.statement: A category with cofibrations has a distinguished zero object, isomorphisms and all 0 → A are cofibrations, and pushouts along cofibrations exist with cofibrations stable under cobase change (W0–W2); a Waldhausen category adds a subcategory of weak equivalences containing isomorphisms and satisfying the gluing axiom (W3). S_nC is the category of functors A: Ar[n] → C, (i, j) ↦ A_{i,j}, with A_{j,j} = 0, every A_{i,j} → A_{i,k} a cofibration and A_{i,j} ↣ A_{i,k} ↠ A_{j,k} a cofibration sequence; equivalently sequences of cofibrations A_{0,1} ↣ ⋯ ↣ A_{0,n} with chosen subquotients. A morphism of S_nC is a cofibration when for all i < j < k the induced map of cofibration sequences is a cofibration in S₂C (the components on sub and quotient objects and the map A′_{i,j} ∪_{A_{i,j}} A_{i,k} → A′_{i,k} are cofibrations), and a weak equivalence when it is objectwise a weak equivalence. [n] ↦ S_nC is a simplicial Waldhausen category; K(C) = Ω|wS.C| with |wS₀C| a point, BwC → Ω|wS.C| from the 1-skeleton, and π₁|wS.C| ≅ K₀(C).
hypotheses: C small; exact functors preserve zero, cofibrations, weak equivalences and pushouts along cofibrations.

Cofibrations of S_nC are defined by a latching condition, not objectwise: for all i < j < k the induced map of cofibration sequences must be a cofibration of S₂C, i.e. the comparison maps A′_{i,j} ∪_{A_{i,j}} A_{i,k} → A′_{i,k} are cofibrations (Weibel IV 8.2–8.3; Schlichting A.6 for finite posets). That objectwise cofibrations would not suffice is the roadmap's warning, not a statement proved in these sources.
Saturation, extension and cylinder axioms are extra hypotheses needed only by later theorems.

Define the extension category S₂C = E(C) with its cofibrations and weak equivalences (Weibel II 9.3, IV 8.2) and S_nC with choices of subquotients (Weibel IV Definition 8.3; Waldhausen §1.3).

Faces delete a row and column of the staircase (∂₀ quotients by A_{0,1}), degeneracies duplicate; they are exact (Weibel IV Definition 8.3.1 and Exercises 8.1–8.2, stated as exercises; Waldhausen refers to the lemmas of §1.1 upon inspection).

nodes.statement: For a category C with cofibrations and weak equivalences, the map wS.E(C) → wS.C × wS.C, (A ↣ C ↠ B) ↦ (A, B), is a homotopy equivalence. nodes.title: Relative S.-construction fibration and the delooping |wS.C| ≃ Ω|wS.S.C|
nodes.statement: For an exact functor f: A → B of categories with cofibrations and weak equivalences, let S.(f: A → B) be the pullback of S.A → S.B ← PS.B. Then wS.B → wS.S.(f) → wS.S.A is a fibration up to homotopy. In particular (f = id) wS.C → P(wS.S.C) → wS.S.C is one, so |wS.C| ≃ Ω|wS.S.C| and |wS.^{(n)}C| ≃ Ω|wS.^{(n+1)}C| for n ≥ 1; for exact functors A → B → C the square with wS.B → wS.S.(A → B) over wS.C → wS.S.(A → C) is homotopy cartesian; wS.B → wS.C → wS.S.(B → C) is a fibration sequence; and a retract C of B splits wS.B ≃ wS.C × wS.S.(C → B).

Uses the fibration criterion for simplicial spaces with connected base terms (Waldhausen 1978, Lemma 5.2), which was not read.
proofSteps: Lemma 1.5.1: the path object PX of a simplicial object is simplicially homotopy equivalent to the constant object X₀, with an explicit homotopy; hence |P(wS.C)| is contractible and wC → P(wS.C) → wS.C gives |wC| → Ω|wS.C| (Waldhausen §1.5).
Proposition 1.5.5: by the fibration criterion it suffices that for each n, wS.B → wS.S_n(f) → wS.S_nA is a fibration up to homotopy, the base being connected.

nodes.title: Waldhausen localization (fibration) theorem
nodes.statement: Let A be a category with cofibrations with two categories of weak equivalences v(A) ⊂ w(A), both making A a Waldhausen category, and let A^w be the Waldhausen subcategory (A^w, v) of objects A with 0 → A in w. If (A, w) has a cylinder functor satisfying the cylinder axiom and w satisfies saturation and extension, then K(A^w) → K(A, v) → K(A, w) is a homotopy fibration with long exact sequence ending in K₀(A^w) → K₀(A, v) → K₀(A, w) → 0. Schlichting's variant replaces the cylinder functor by the requirement that every map factor as a cofibration followed by a map in w; then vS.C^w → wS.C^w ≃ * over vS.C → wS.C is homotopy cartesian.
hypotheses: v ⊂ w; cylinder functor with cylinder axiom for (A, w); w saturated and satisfies the extension axiom.
Schlichting A.3: factorization of every map into a cofibration followed by a map in w, plus saturation and extension for w.
proofSteps: Form the bicategory v.w.C of squares with vertical maps in v and horizontal maps in w; wC → v.w.C is a homotopy equivalence (swallowing lemma, Weibel IV 3.10.2 and Exercise 3.13), and similarly for S_nC.

The sub-bicategory v.co w.C whose horizontal maps are also cofibrations is homotopy equivalent to v.w.C, using saturation and the cylinder axiom on each C(m, v) (Weibel's proof cites IV Exercise 8.14, but the statement used, co wC ≃ wC for a saturated category with a cylinder functor satisfying the cylinder axiom, is IV Exercise 8.15, stated with a hint; Schlichting A.11 replaces this by the factorization hypothesis).
By the extension axiom trivial cofibrations are cofibrations with quotient in C^w, giving S_n(f) ≃ co w_nC for f: (C^w, v) → (C, v) and vS.S.f ≃ v.co w.S.C.

The top row vS.C^w → vS.C → v.co w.S.C is thus the relative S.-construction fibration (previous node), and the square compares it with wS.C ≃ v.w.S.C (Weibel V Theorem 2.1 proof); Schlichting's proof replaces Waldhausen 1.6.3 by A.11 in Waldhausen's proof of 1.6.4, which was not read.

nodes.title: Waldhausen approximation theorem
nodes.statement: Let F: A → B be an exact functor between saturated Waldhausen categories such that (a) a map of A is a weak equivalence iff its image is, and (App) every map F(A) → B factors as F(a) for a map (which may be taken to be a cofibration) a: A → A′ followed by a weak equivalence F(A′) ≃ B. If A has a cylinder functor satisfying the cylinder axiom (Waldhausen), or merely every map of A factors as a cofibration followed by a weak equivalence (Schlichting), then wA → wB and wS.A → wS.B are homotopy equivalences and K(A) ≃ K(B).
hypotheses: Saturation of both categories; (App) including the detection of weak equivalences; cylinder functor with cylinder axiom or the factorization property in A.
The theorem can fail without cylinders or factorizations: A_⊕ ⊂ A satisfies (App) but K₀ differs (Weibel V Remark 2.4.2).
proofSteps: (App) passes to S_nA → S_nB (Weibel V Exercise 2.1; Waldhausen 1.6.6, cited by Schlichting, not read), so it suffices to prove wF: wA → wB is a homotopy equivalence and realize (Weibel V Theorem 2.4 proof).
By Theorem A it suffices that each comma category (F ↓ B) is contractible; it is non-empty by factoring ∅ → B (Schlichting A.2 proof).

Criterion A.10: a non-empty category is contractible if every functor from a finite poset to it is null-homotopic, since Sd² of a finite simplicial set is the nerve of a finite poset (Thomason 1980, cited).

Given P → (F ↓ B), factor ∅ → X as a cofibration followed by a weak equivalence in the diagram category (A.9), take colim_P Y (exists by A.7, preserved by F), factor colim F(Y) → B by (App), and use saturation to get a null-homotopy X ← Y → cZ.
Weibel's own proof omits the five-page simplicial argument and refers to Waldhausen 1.6.7; the decomposed proof here is Schlichting's.
acceptance: K(A) ≃ KCh^b(A) ≃ KCh^{hb}_±(A) ≃ KCh^{hb}(A) for abelian A (Weibel V 2.7.1).
K(R) ≃ KCh^b(P(R)) ≃ KCh_perf(R) (Weibel V 2.7.2), and K(X) = KCh_perf(X) agrees with KVB(X) when every coherent sheaf is a quotient of a vector bundle (2.7.3).

For a saturated Waldhausen category with a cylinder functor satisfying the cylinder axiom, enlarging the cofibrations co ⊂ co₁ with the same weak equivalences (so that (A, co₁, w) is still a Waldhausen category) does not change K-theory (Weibel V 2.5.1, Hinich–Shektman, by approximation).

nodes.title: Gillet–Waldhausen: K(A) ≃ KCh^b(A)
nodes.statement: Let A be an exact category closed under kernels of surjections in an ambient abelian category, and Ch^b(A) the Waldhausen category of bounded complexes with degreewise admissible monomorphisms as cofibrations and quasi-isomorphisms (computed in the ambient abelian category) as weak equivalences. Then A ⊂ Ch^b(A) induces K(A) ≃ KCh^b(A). Without closure under kernels, Weibel V Remark 2.2.1 still gives K(A) ≃ KCh^b(A) provided quasi-isomorphisms are computed in the category L of left exact functors: the subcategory A′ of the idempotent completion Â with class in K₀(A) is closed under admissible epimorphisms in L, Theorem 2.2 applies to A′, and Waldhausen cofinality gives K(A) ≃ K(A′) and KCh^b(A) ≃ KCh^b(A′). The split-cofibration structure on Ch^b(A) has the same K-theory.
hypotheses: A closed under kernels of surjections in its ambient abelian category (otherwise K₀(A) may differ from K₀Ch^b(A)); weak equivalences are quasi-isomorphisms in the ambient abelian category, not chain homotopy equivalences.
Uses Waldhausen localization with a cylinder functor on Ch^b(A) (mapping cylinder, Weibel IV Example 8.8.3).
proofSteps: For a ≤ b, Ch^{[a,b]} with isomorphisms as weak equivalences has as its category of acyclic objects the admissibly exact complexes A^{[a,b]}_exact, using closure under kernels of surjections (Weibel V Exercise 2.4).

By additivity, K(A^{[a,b]}_exact) ≃ K(A)^{b−a} and K(iso Ch^{[a,b]}) ≃ K(A)^{b−a+1} ('forget differentials', Exercises 1.5–1.6), the map between them being induced by (B_{a+1}, …, B_b) ↦ (B_{a+1}, B_{a+1} ⊕ B_{a+2}, …, B_b), whose homotopy cofibre is K(A) via the Euler characteristic.

Pass to the colimit over a → −∞, b → ∞ and apply Waldhausen localization to iso Ch^b ⊂ quasi-isomorphisms to identify the cofibre with KCh^b(A) (Weibel V Theorem 2.2 proof, following Thomason–Trobaugh 1.11.7).

Remark 2.2.1: via the Yoneda embedding into left exact functors L (quasi-isomorphisms computed in L), K₀-cofinality (II.7.2, 9.4), Exercise IV.8.13 and Waldhausen cofinality IV.8.9 remove the kernel-closure hypothesis.
acceptance: K₀Ch^b(A) ≅ K₀(A) with [C] = Σ(−1)^i[C_i] (Weibel II Theorem 9.2.2) as the degree-zero check.
splitCh^b(A) → Ch^b(A) is a K-equivalence (Weibel V Exercise 2.3, exercise-level).
Do not replace quasi-isomorphisms by chain homotopy equivalences without a separate argument for the category used.

nodes.title: Relative K-theory, support K-theory and the excision boundary
nodes.statement: For a ring homomorphism f: R → R′, K(f) is the homotopy fibre of K(R) → K(R′), with long exact sequence ⋯ → K_{n+1}(R′) → K_n(f) → K_n(R) → K_n(R′) → ⋯ → K₁(R′) → K₀(f) → K₀(R) → K₀(R′); all K_n(f), including K₀(f), are abelian groups via the functorial H-space structure. For an ideal I, K(R, I) = K(R → R/I), with K₀(R, I) ≅ K₀(I) and K₁(R, I) the classical relative group. For an exact functor f: B → C of Waldhausen categories, K(f) = Ω²|wS.(S.f)| fits into a long exact sequence ending K₀(B) → K₀(C) → K₋₁(f) → 0. Support K-theory for a central multiplicatively closed set S is K(R on S) = KCh^b_S(P(R)) (bounded complexes of finitely generated projectives with S⁻¹P exact). It is a different construction from the homotopy fibre, and Weibel V Theorem 2.6.3 proves that K(R on S) → K(R) → K(S⁻¹R) is a homotopy fibration ending in K₀(R on S) → K₀(R) → K₀(S⁻¹R); the cokernel of K₀(R) → K₀(S⁻¹R) is not seen by the connective fibre (Waldhausen's relative theory records it as K₋₁(f)), and the category H_S(R) of S-torsion perfect modules need not model the fibre when S contains zero divisors (Weibel V Exercise 2.9). Excision is not automatic: a nonunital ring I satisfies absolute excision for K₁ iff I = I², and (Suslin) for K_n iff Tor^{Z⊕I}_i(Z, Z) = 0 for i = 1, …, n; H-unital rings satisfy excision in all degrees.
hypotheses: Unital rings and ring homomorphisms for K(f); nonunital I is treated through the augmented ring Z ⊕ I.
The excision criteria are quoted from Suslin 1995 and Suslin–Wodzicki 1992 without proof in the source read.

nodes.title: Schlichting's set-up for negative K-groups and localization in negative degrees
nodes.statement: A sequence A → B → C of small triangulated categories is exact if the composite is zero, A → B is fully faithful and B/A → C is cofinal (fully faithful, every object a direct summand of one in the image). Given a category of models M with D: M → (small triangulated categories) and functors id → F → S preserving exact sequences with IK₀(FM) = 0 and M → FM → SM exact, define IK₀(M) = K₀ of the idempotent completion of DM and IK_{−n}(M) = IK₀(S^nM). An exact sequence A → B → C in M then gives an exact sequence ⋯ → IK_i(A) → IK_i(B) → IK_i(C) → IK_{i−1}(A) → ⋯ for i ≤ 0, and a map with cofinal D(f) induces isomorphisms on IK_i, i ≤ 0. IK_{−1}(M) = 0 iff for every exact sequence M → N → P in M the Verdier quotient D̃N/D̃M of the idempotent completions is idempotent complete (Remark 1.9).
hypotheses: Models are required: the construction is for triangulated categories with a chosen model in M, not for arbitrary triangulated categories.

Uses three facts: the idempotent completion of a triangulated category is triangulated (Balmer–Schlichting), dense subcategories correspond to subgroups of K₀ (Thomason 1997), and exact sequences give exact IK₀ sequences (SGA 5 VIII 3.1); these were not read.
proofSteps: Form the 3×3 diagram of idempotent completions of D applied to A → B → C, F(−) and S(−) with exact rows and columns; DFM is idempotent complete because IK₀(FM) = 0 (Schlichting 1.5).

Define δ: IK₀(C) → IK₀(SA) by lifting c to B in DFB with p_F(B) ≅ i_C(c) and setting δ(c) = [p_B(B)]; independence of the lift uses IK₀(FA) = 0, and distinguished triangles give additivity (Lemma 1.6).
Exactness at IK₀(C) and IK₋₁(A) by diagram chases using Thomason's classification (Theorem 1.7 proof); negative degrees follow by applying the case i = 0 to S^i.
Corollary 1.8 applies 1.7 to 0 → A → B; Remark 1.9 characterizes IK₋₁.
acceptance: For central non-zero-divisors S in R, the sequence IK₀(A) → IK₀(R) → IK₀(S⁻¹R) → IK₋₁(A) → ⋯ with A the S-torsion modules of projective dimension ≤ 1 recovers Carter's sequence (Schlichting 5.5).
The first map in the K₀ sequence need not be injective nor the last surjective (Schlichting 1.2).

nodes.title: Frobenius pairs, the flasque countable envelope and the suspension functor
nodes.statement: A Frobenius pair A = (A, A₀) is a fully faithful inclusion of small Frobenius categories preserving projective-injectives; its derived category is the Verdier quotient DA = stable(A)/stable(A₀). The countable envelope FE of an exact category (sequences of inflations, Hom = lim_i colim_j) is exact, has exact countable coproducts, and is flasque (T ⊕ id ≅ T with T = ⊕_{i≥0} t^i). For a Frobenius pair, FA = (FA, FA₀) is a Frobenius pair, DA → DFA is fully faithful, DFA has countable coproducts and is c-compactly generated by DA, and the idempotent completion of DA is the c-compact part of DFA. The suspension SA = (FA, S₀A), with S₀A the objects vanishing in DFA/DA, satisfies DSA = DFA/DA, and id → F → S satisfies Set-up 1.3 on the category of Frobenius pairs. For an exact category E, (Ch^bE, Ac^bE) with degreewise split conflations is a Frobenius pair with derived category D^b(E), and IK_i(E) := IK_i(Ch^bE, Ac^bE).
hypotheses: Small Frobenius categories; maps of Frobenius pairs are exact functors preserving projective-injective objects and the subcategories.

c-compactness means Hom(X, −) commutes with countable coproducts; Theorem 2.9 (a variant of Neeman 1992) requires T c-compactly generated and R ⊂ T a c-compactly generated full triangulated subcategory closed under countable coproducts with R^c ⊂ T^c.
proofSteps: Homotopy colimits in triangulated categories with countable coproducts and Hom out of c-compact objects commuting with them (Schlichting 2.2–2.4); Lemma 2.6 and Corollaries 2.7, 2.10; Theorem 2.9 with proof via calculus of fractions.
Countable envelope and flasqueness (Lemma 4.2 with explicit T and natural isomorphism A ⊕ TA ≅ TA).
Proposition 4.4: A is c-compact in FA ⊂ Lex A and colim A_i = hocolim A_i by the sequence ⊕A_i → ⊕A_i → colim A_i; the pair case follows from Theorem 2.9.
Theorem 4.8: IK₀(FA) = 0 because DFA has countable coproducts; F preserves exact sequences by 4.4, 4.6, 2.10; S by Lemma 2.11.

Examples 5.3–5.4: chain complexes with degreewise split conflations form a Frobenius category whose projective-injectives are the contractible complexes; the homotopy category modulo acyclics is D^b(E).
acceptance: IK₀(E) = K₀(E) for idempotent complete E and K₀ of the idempotent completion otherwise (Schlichting 5.5).

nodes.title: The nonconnective K-theory spectrum of a Frobenius pair
nodes.statement: For a Frobenius pair A with K(A) = Ω|wS.A| (cofibrations the inflations, weak equivalences the maps invertible in DA), the spaces K(A), K(SA), K(S²A), … with maps K(A) → ΩK(SA) from the square K(A) → K(A, A) ≃ * over * ≃ K(FA) → K(SA) form a spectrum IK(A) with ΩIK(A) an Ω-spectrum, π_i IK(A) = K_i(A) for i > 0, π₀ = K₀ of the idempotent completion of DA, and π_i = IK_i(A) for i < 0. An exact sequence of Frobenius pairs gives a homotopy cartesian square IK(A) → IK(B) over * → IK(C) and a long exact sequence in all degrees. A map of Frobenius pairs inducing an equivalence DA → DB induces a homotopy equivalence K(A) → K(B); a cofinal D(f) induces isomorphisms on π_i, i > 0, and a monomorphism on π₀. For an exact category E, π_i IK(E) are Quillen's K-groups for i > 0.
hypotheses: Additive categories are strictified to have unital associative sums (May 1974, cited).
Derived invariance needs a map of models (Frobenius pairs); an abstract triangulated equivalence is not enough (models are essential, Schlichting's introduction citing Schlichting 2002).
proofSteps: K(FA) is contractible functorially: the flasque functor T and the functorial homotopy between loop and H-space multiplications give id ≃ * (Lemma 11.3); K(A, A) is contractible since each S_n(A, A) has an initial object.
Cofinality 11.17: reduce to the subcategory B₁ with objects in the image of DA, apply 11.15 and cofinality A.4.
Fibration 11.18: apply the fibration theorem A.3 to the change of weak equivalences from (B, B₀) to (B, B₁), using that Frobenius pairs have factorizations (11.2).
Theorem 11.7: with Â the pair whose derived category is the idempotent completion, 11.17 and 11.18 give K(Â) ≃ ΩK(SA) ≃ ΩK((SA)^), so ΩIK is an Ω-spectrum and the homotopy groups are as stated.

Proposition 11.15: translate Thomason–Trobaugh 1.9.8 to Frobenius pairs: the category C of (A, F(A) ↣ B) with B/F(A) acyclic retracts onto A, and C → B is a K-equivalence by the dual approximation property, verified by homotopy-commutative diagram manipulations.

Theorem 11.10 localization in all degrees for D^b(A) → D^b(B) → D^b(C) exact; resolution-type derived equivalences give isomorphisms in all degrees.

nodes.title: Agreement with Bass/Thomason negative K-groups and vanishing theorems
nodes.statement: IK_i(R) agrees with Bass's (and Pedersen's) K_i(R) for rings R, IK_i(X) with Thomason's K_i^B(X) for quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes, and IK_i(A) with Karoubi's and Pedersen–Weibel's groups for additive categories, i ≤ 0. IK₋₁(E) is the monoid of isomorphism classes of idempotents of the unbounded derived category D(E) modulo those that split; IK₋₁(A) = 0 for every small abelian category; IK_i(A) = 0 for i < 0 for every small noetherian abelian category; consequently K_i(R) = 0 for i < 0 when finitely generated R-modules form a noetherian abelian category derived-equivalent to projectives (regular noetherian R), and negative G-theory of a noetherian scheme vanishes.
hypotheses: Agreement for schemes (hence commutative rings) rests on Thomason's projective bundle theorem [Tho93] and the proof of Bass's fundamental theorem in Thomason–Trobaugh 6.6(b); agreement for not necessarily commutative rings goes through the additive-category case, which rests on Cárdenas–Pedersen [CP97] and on Karoubi [Kar71] and Pedersen [Ped84] identifying their groups with Bass's. None of these was read.

The proof of Theorem 9.3 uses the noetherian hypothesis (A[t] noetherian; injective envelopes of noetherian objects in Lemma 9.4). nodes.title: Equivalence, Morita, product and filtered-colimit invariance
nodes.statement: Exact equivalences induce K-equivalences; Morita equivalent rings have equivalent P(R) ≃ P(S) and M(R) ≃ M(S), hence K_n(R) ≅ K_n(S) and G_n(R) ≅ G_n(S); in particular K(M_r(A)) ≃ K(A). K-theory takes finite products of exact categories and rings to products and commutes with filtered colimits of exact categories (and of rings via idempotent matrices); IK_n commutes with filtered colimits of Frobenius pairs for n ≤ 0 (Schlichting Lemma 6.3; positive degrees are not treated there). At the enhanced level, a map of Frobenius pairs inducing an equivalence of derived categories induces an equivalence of K-theory spectra.
hypotheses: Morita invariance is induced by an actual equivalence of exact categories; derived invariance requires a map of models, not a bare triangulated equivalence.
Filtered colimits over small filtering index categories.

nodes.title: External products from biexact functors
nodes.statement: A biexact functor ⊗: A × B → C of exact categories (partial functors exact, A ⊗ 0 = 0 ⊗ B = 0) induces QA ⊗ QB → QQC, a map BQA ∧ BQB → BQQC and bilinear products K_i(A) ⊗ K_j(B) → K_{i+j}(C) via the reduced join and Waldhausen's delooping BQA ≃ ΩBQQA. For Waldhausen categories a biexact functor satisfying the admissibility condition (F(A′, B) ∪_{F(A, B)} F(A, B′) → F(A′, B′) a cofibration) induces |wS.A| ∧ |wS.B| → |wwS.S.C|. For a commutative ring R (or scheme X), tensor product makes K_*(R) (K_*(X)) a graded-commutative ring with unit and G_*(A) a K_*(R)-module; transfers satisfy projection formulas. The K₀ product agrees with the classical product.
